title: Gideon and the Homecoming
premise: Odile Vane bakes her feelings into bread — grief, hope, fury — and counts the days until graduation like a sentence. When her history teacher pairs her with Gideon Marsh, the boy whose family's development company bulldozed her grandmother's orchard, for a semester project on local justice, their rivalry curdles into something neither expected: a partnership, then a friendship, then a slow-burning love neither will name. Together they uncover that Gideon's grandfather stole the Vane land through forged deeds, and Odile must choose between exposing him publicly at the county fair championship or letting Gideon make amends his own way. In the end, she wins the baking championship that doesn't matter, loses the one that does on purpose, and the land is returned not by law but by choice — while prom becomes the homecoming neither of them saw coming.
about_author: Tamsin Crane grew up above her aunt's bakery in a small river town where every dispute was settled over cinnamon rolls and grudges. She writes stories about stubborn kids who fix what adults broke, usually with flour on their hands.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the first day of senior year, Odile bakes her dread into a loaf of sourdough and serves detention-worthy attitude in homeroom. We learn her grandmother lost the orchard to the Marsh Development Company three years ago and died before the appeal finished. Emotional beat: restless anger looking for a target.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mr. Okonkwo announces the semester-long 'Justice in Our Town' project and reads pairings aloud: Vane and Marsh. The class goes silent; Gideon smirks like it's a joke at her expense. She throws a roll at his head and earns Saturday detention — with him. Beat: open war declared.

chapters.title: Detention Loaves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Stuck together in the empty home ec room, they negotiate a truce: divide the project, never speak outside class. Gideon reveals he didn't know about the orchard until Odile's outburst made him look it up. Beat: grudging curiosity replacing hatred.

chapters.title: What the Deed Says
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Researching his own family for the project, Gideon finds the 1998 deed transfer in his grandfather's files — and a signature that doesn't match Odile's great-grandmother's handwriting on anything else. He sits with the forgery all night. Beat: the ground shifts under him.

chapters.title: Flour War
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A late-night library session collapses into a flour fight in the home ec room after hours, laughing until they can't breathe. Her best friend Priya notices Odile came home smelling like someone else's cologne. Beat: the first crack in the wall of hate.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The county fair baking championship entries open; Odile has won juniors twice but this year the prize includes seed money she could use to buy back a corner of the orchard. Gideon offers to be her taste-tester. Beat: stakes become personal and practical.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Study
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon confronts his grandfather, who dismisses the deed as 'old business' and threatens to pull Gideon's college fund if he keeps digging. Gideon photographs everything anyway. Beat: inheritance revealed as a cage, not a gift.

chapters.title: Rye for Rage
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's father's bakery faces eviction from — of course — a Marsh-owned building. She bakes a rye so bitter customers send it back, and Gideon eats a whole slice without flinching and says, 'Tell me.' Beat: he chooses her side without being asked.

chapters.title: The Other Championship
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The spring mock trial championship approaches — the one that actually matters for Gideon's pre-law future and his grandfather's pride. His team needs him fully committed just as the project demands more time. Beat: two clocks start ticking against each other.

chapters.title: Orchard Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They sneak onto the fenced-off orchard land; Gideon sees the stump lines, the well, the swing set his company left standing. Odile tells the story of her grandmother's last harvest. He apologizes — really apologizes — for the first time. Beat: guilt becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Working late on the project, an almost-kiss interrupted by Priya bursting in with news: the county archive has the original 1998 survey map proving the boundary was falsified. Beat: longing deferred, evidence gained.

chapters.title: Team Marsh
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Gideon's mock trial teammates discover his research folder and accuse him of sabotaging his own family; his grandfather hears rumors and shows up at the bakery to buy silence with a check. Odile watches Gideon refuse it. Beat: public loyalty, private cost.

chapters.title: Cold Oven
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile learns Gideon initially took the project assignment as a chance to 'manage' her — a text from his old friend surfaces. She freezes him out; the bread comes out flat for a week. Beat: betrayal, real or misread.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Searching the study again, Gideon finds his grandfather's own confession letter — unsent, decades old — admitting the fraud and naming Odile's grandmother by name. He realizes his grandfather has been waiting to be caught. Beat: horror and strange mercy.

chapters.title: Reconciliation Dough
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Gideon shows Odile the letter; she reads her grandmother's name in a stranger's handwriting and cries into the proofing dough. They plan: return the land quietly before graduation, no scandal, no trial. Beat: forgiveness and shared purpose.

chapters.title: Mock Trial Semifinals
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon deliberately argues the opposing side's weakness — property fraud — so convincingly his coach suspects he's throwing it. His grandfather attends and understands exactly what Gideon did. Beat: the first championship sacrificed on purpose.

chapters.title: Promposal, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Gideon stages an elaborate promposal in the bakery window; Odile, mid-panic about fair finals, says yes before he finishes. Priya films it; the whole school knows by lunch. Beat: joy, finally, unguarded.

chapters.title: Fair Day
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the county fair, Odile's entry — a braided loaf based on her grandmother's recipe, baked with Gideon beside her — wins the championship that doesn't matter. The seed money is enough for one acre, not the whole orchard. Beat: triumph shadowed by arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Grandfather's Choice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Cornered by Gideon's semifinal performance and the letter, the grandfather signs the land back — not out of goodness, he says, but because 'a legacy built on a lie isn't a legacy.' He disowns Gideon's inheritance anyway. Beat: justice outside the law, at terrible price.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Prom in the restored orchard barn, fairy lights in the old apple trees, the whole found-family crew — Priya, Mr. Okonkwo, even the rival teammates. Odile and Gideon dance under the trees her grandmother planted. Beat: homecoming in every sense.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Graduation morning; the Vanes replant the first saplings. Gideon, cut off financially, has a scholarship and a job offer at the bakery. He gives Odile the confession letter to keep or burn; she frames it instead. Beat: inheritance redefined as what you build, not what you're given.

chapters.title: Bread for Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing. Summer's first morning: Odile bakes a loaf with no grief in it at all — just yeast, salt, patience, and something new. She writes 'Vane & Marsh' on the bakery's chalkboard special. Beat: quiet, earned hope; the story ends where it began, at the oven, changed.
